question: During the ancient period in India, the term 'sandhi-vigrahika' was used to refer to which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Minister of war and peace**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the reign of Samudragupta, the meaning of Sandhi-Vigrahika was Minister of War and Peace.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In Ancient India, the Gupta Dynasty was founded by Sri Gupta.
 
• Samudragupta was a famous ruler of a dynasty known as the Guptas.
 
• We know about Samudragupta from a long inscription actually a poem in Sanskrit, composed by his court poet Harisena.
 
• This was inscribed on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.
 
• This inscription is of the special kind known as prashasti, a Sanskrit word, meaning ‘in praise of.
 
• The poet praised the king in glowing terms as a warrior, as a king who won victories in battle, who was learned, and the best of poets.
 
• He is also described as equal to the gods
